outcome: No proof, disproof, or partial resolution of Beal's conjecture has been established since 26 January 2024; only a steady stream of unrefereed amateur preprints claiming proofs, none accepted by the mathematical community, and Andrew Beal's $1 million prize remains unclaimed.

counterexample.verified_how: Extensive computational search (per Durango Bill's site and Norvig's earlier search) has found no counterexamples with C^Z up to at least 1.0E30 assuming an exponent > 4; no new counterexample search results found in the window.

summary: Beal's conjecture (A^x + B^y = C^z with x,y,z > 2 implies A, B, C share a common prime factor) remains open as of 26 September 2026. Wikipedia's article on the conjecture, checked directly, still describes it as unsolved, notes the $1 million Beal Prize (held in trust by the AMS) is unclaimed, and records only that the conjecture has been verified for many specific exponent cases and that the abc conjecture (itself unproven) would imply only finitely many counterexamples exist. In the 26 January 2024 - present window I found a large number of self-published, non-peer-reviewed preprints claiming proofs, all on venues with no mathematical vetting: SSRN ('Machine Learning Guided Proof of Beal's Conjecture', Jonathan Wilson, 11 March 2024; 'Beal's Conjecture: A Rigorous Proof', Jonathan Wilson, 30 June 2024 — explicitly a revision addressing the first paper's 'unproven lemmas, reliance on empirical data, circular reasoning, incomplete contradictions, misuse of number theory results, and lack of generality'), Preprints.org ('The Germany Problem for Beal's Conjecture', Feb 2024; 'Elementary Proof of Beal's Conjecture [v2]', Jan 2025), Zenodo ('A theoretical counterexample proof of Beal Conjecture', dated July 2026, which argues only that counterexamples 'should exist' and where to search for them computationally, without exhibiting one), ResearchGate, Academia.edu, ScienceOpen/HAL, and a small predatory-adjacent journal (IJDR, Mathematical Journal). None of these has been digested by an expert, accepted by a journal of record, or referenced by any mainstream number theorist; searches for commentary from figures such as Terence Tao turned up nothing specific to Beal's conjecture. The Wilson SSRN paper is the only item that invokes machine learning at all, and its own abstract describes ML only as having helped surface empirical patterns ('key lemmas derived with the help of patterns discovered through computational experiments') that guided a human-authored argument which the same author later needed to substantially rewrite to fix logical flaws — this is not an authors'-own-account claim that an AI system produced any piece of the mathematics that survived into a checked result, and no such result was ever accepted as correct. I also checked Google DeepMind's formal-conjectures Lean repository (arXiv 2605.13171 and the GitHub repo/README) since it is a legitimate AI-adjacent project formalizing conjecture statements for benchmarking; I could not confirm via search or the fetched README whether Beal's conjecture is among its ~2615 formalized statements, but even if present, that project formalizes statements only (not proofs) for benchmark use and would not itself constitute progress on the problem. No credible AI-generated or AI-assisted proof, counterexample, or bound exists for this problem in the window; the conjecture is exactly as open now as on 26 January 2024.
competing_reading: One could argue the Wilson SSRN papers deserve 'claimed' status with 'ai_role: assisted' given their title explicitly invokes machine learning guidance. I reject this because (a) SSRN is not a refereed mathematics venue and hosts unvetted user submissions, (b) the author's own second paper acknowledges the first contained circular reasoning and unproven lemmas, i.e. it was not a valid proof even by its author's later admission, and (c) the abstract describes ML's role as pattern-spotting in computational experiments that fed a human-constructed argument, not as producing mathematics that appears in a valid final result — since no valid final result exists, there is nothing for the AI role to attach to.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or announcement, from this window, that is digested by a professional number theorist, accepted at a refereed venue, or produces an explicit, verified counterexample or a machine-checked (and expert-reviewed) Lean/Coq proof; absent that, continued monitoring of arXiv number theory listings and the Wikipedia article's revision history would be the way to catch any future change.
